- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively, especially if recent lows are broken.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a lag correction: delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 30-day mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- In sentiment-neutral or mixed periods, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 18-day rolling mean as baseline, not 30-day forecast.
